messages:
maria: Heads up — after the 1768 runtime rollout (kernel v3.14, fused-attn change) we saw a sharp drop in prefix/KV cache hit-rate for the customer benchmarks. numbers from last night: hit-rate ~92% -> ~38% for the 512-prefix workload. p50 latency for cached requests +5ms, p99 +120ms.
jon: Oof. Is this correlated with quant profile changes or just the kernel swap?
devon: I profiled a sample trace — the cache key hashing looks unchanged, but the ordering of key metadata in the kernel's KV emit changed. basically the kernel now emits (layer,head,seq) vs old (layer,seq,head) which broke the cache key normalization in runtime-adapter.
ryan: That would produce consistent misses even if the actual KV contents were identical. Any quick repro?
maria: Yes — repro on local with model v2.7 (LLM-small) using the new runtime binary:
```
# reproduce script
python perf/repro_prefix_cache.py --model llm-small --seq 512 --warmup 50 --requests 1000
# compare hit-rate in logs: cache.hit / cache.requests
```

alice: I ran the repro and grabbed traces. The cache_key string inside runtime-adapter shows different serialize orders. Example: new: "l3:s7:h0" old: "l3:h0:s7" — so the hashing function is stable but the field order changed.
devon: This matches the kernel change PR (runtime/kernel#412) — they switched some attention tensor packing for fused-attn microkernel performance. unintended side effect is different metadata emission.
maria: Impact summary from staging:
- 38% effective hit-rate on prefix-heavy traffic
- 2.1x token compute increase on those requests
- QoS: p99 token-latency spike to ~420ms on small instance types
- Affected: hosted and dedicated customers using pinned model v2.7+ with long prompts
jon: What are mitigation options? Short-term roll-back of kernel? Patch on runtime-adapter to normalize field ordering? Warmup-only workaround?
ryan: Short term: add a normalization shim in runtime-adapter that parses the kernel metadata and reorders fields into canonical key before hashing. Cheap and low-risk.
alice: I can open a quick PR for normalization. Will also add a fuzzy match to treat swapped-order keys as hits for a 24h window to recover traffic.
devon: Longer-term: kernel should stop assuming external ordering or emit a structured proto instead of string blobs. File bug with kernel team and link PR that changed packing.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of runtime-adapter/normalize-key v0.1 scheduled at 2026-03-18T02:00Z to region us-west-2. :gear:
maria: Also we noticed warmup strategy previously relied on sequential prefix warming that assumed stable keying. If we opt for normalization shim, warmup will still need to re-run since many cached entries were lost when the rollout happened. Suggest running a targeted warmup job for top 20 prefixes per customer.
jon: Agree. ops: can we schedule warmup job post-canary? If we push the normalization shim, we can rehydrate cache faster and avoid serving misses in canary.
ryan: I'll wire a warmup pipeline that loads top prefixes from metrics and issues authenticated dry-run requests to fill cache. It will rate-limit to not disturb customers.
alice: PR opened: runtime-adapter#1789 — includes normalization + fuzz-match and unit tests. small perf cost (~0.4% CPU) but recovers hit-rate.
devon: Kernel team response: runtime/kernel#413 — acknowledged and reverting the metadata ordering change for v3.15, working on a structured metadata emitter for v3.16.
maria: Plan of action:
1) Canary deploy normalization shim (runtime-adapter vX) in us-west-2 (ops-bot scheduled).
2) Run targeted warmup job for affected customers (ryan).
3) If canary shows hit-rate recovery >85% within 1 hour, roll to global.
4) Kernel team to revert ordering in v3.15 and add structured metadata for v3.16.
5) Postmortem and add a regression test that fuzzes kernel metadata ordering.

jon: Any telemetry queries we should run to quantify rollout blast radius?
maria: Run these: 
- metrics.cache.prefix_hit_rate{model=~"llm-small|llm-medium"}
- logs.runtime.cache_key_variants | top 50 by count
- profile.cpu.per_token by instance_type

alice: I'll add a dashboard and an alert: if prefix_hit_rate drops >15% from baseline for 10m, page on-call.
devon: Note for postmortem: check whether quantization profile changes in the model packaging also altered tensor layout — we saw one model edge that emitted different layer ordering when using q4_0 vs q8_0. Might be two simultaneous regressions.
maria: Good call. Devon — can you run the quick cross-check between q4_0 and q8_0 on the same kernel? Put results in the incident channel.
devon: On it.
ryan: I'll monitor canary and kick warmup once normalization is live.
alice: small status update after canary (will post here).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary runtime-adapter/normalize-key v0.1 deployed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T02:05Z.
maria: thanks everyone. tagging this thread for the incident postmortem. :white_check_mark:
